units.source_text: 这是高僧容易陷入的弊端。

en.t: This was a weakness into which eminent monks easily fell.

units.source_text: 人们都以为他们有万般的鉴别能力，经常邀请他们去鉴定从人物到书画古董的真伪。

en.t: People all assumed that they possessed every kind of power of discernment, and often invited them to judge the authenticity of things ranging from people to calligraphy, paintings, and antiques.

units.source_text: 有的高僧为了事后不被人耻笑其鉴定错误，就不谈结论性的意见，当然也不会当场提出禅僧式的独断的见解，总给人留下难以捉摸其意思的模棱两可的余地。

en.t: Some eminent monks, in order not to be laughed at afterward for a mistaken appraisal, avoid giving any conclusive opinion; naturally they also refrain from offering a Zen monk's dogmatic judgment on the spot, and always leave people with an ambiguous margin in which their meaning is hard to grasp.

units.source_text: 样海和尚并不是这种人。

en.t: Priest Zenkai was not that kind of person.

units.source_text: 大家知道他会将所见所感都和盘托出的，而对于映现在自己单纯而强烈的目光里的事物，是不会故意去追求什么意义的。

en.t: Everyone knew that he would lay out everything he saw and felt without concealment, and that he would not deliberately go looking for some meaning in the things reflected in his simple yet intense gaze.

units.source_text: 有意义也罢，无意义也罢，禅海和尚使我感到最伟大的，就是他看东西，譬如看我，

en.t: Meaningful or meaningless, what made Priest Zenkai seem greatest to me was that when he looked at things, for example when he looked at me,

units.source_text: 并不想标新立异地以自己的特别目光来看，而是以一般人的目光来看。

en.t: he did not try to look in some novel and peculiar way with his own special gaze, but looked with the eyes of ordinary people.

units.source_text: 对于禅海和尚来说，单纯的主观世界是没有意义的。

en.t: For Priest Zenkai, a purely subjective world had no meaning.

units.source_text: 我懂得禅海和尚想说什么，就渐渐地感到无所顾虑了。

en.t: Once I understood what Priest Zenkai meant to say, I gradually began to feel free of misgivings.

units.source_text: 只要他人把我看成是个平凡的人，我就是平凡的人，

en.t: So long as others regarded me as an ordinary person, I was an ordinary person,

units.source_text: 哪怕胆敢干出多么异常的行动，我的平凡也会像用簸箕来筛米粒一样还是残留着的。

en.t: and no matter how abnormal an act I dared to commit, my ordinariness would still remain, like grains of rice left behind after being sifted in a winnowing basket.
